Republicans in the House of Representatives voted to block the effort to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.  The House approved a procedural motion to refer Republican Congressman Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution to a committee.  Hegseth reacted, calling out  Massie: “Time for one man's final days in Congress to try to do damage to this president. This country and most irresponsibly the warriors who defend it. It's a farce And it's a stunt. And everybody knows it. ”
The vote, which was 211-204, effectively kills the impeachment resolution, for now.  This morning, Hegseth criticized the impeachment effort as being a "political spectacle"

Republican Senator John Thune of South Dakota will be the new Senate Minority Leader.: “I want to see us do is come out of this knowing full well that we took a big electoral defeat but come out swinging. ”
Thune currently serves as Majority Leader, and will assume his new role when the new Democratic-controlled Congress convenes January 3rd.  GOP senators chose Thune, following what's being reported as a contentious hours-long meeting earlier today.

Congressman Jim Jordan of Ohio is the new House Minority Leader.: “Over the next 2 years, House Republicans will fight for American families. When Democrats offer more government, we'll offer more freedom. ”
GOP House members elected Jordan over Louisiana's Steve Scalise as their new leader.  Jordan defeated Scalise by a vote of 106-73.  After the vote, Jordan thanked his colleagues for "their trust," and vowed to keep Democrats in check.

Inflation remains high as new numbers from the Consumer Price Index show...: “It rose in October 0.4%, more than the expected 0.3%. Strip out food and energy and core inflation rose at 0.3%, not the expected 0.2%. No annual comparison this time around because in October last year there was a government shutdown, so nothing to compare it. ”
That's John Terrett reporting.

Former President Joe Biden reveals what President Trump wrote to him upon leaving office in January 2021.
NewsNation's Blake Burman reports: “The New York Times is citing Biden's new memoir, saying that President Trump wrote in part, I know how much you love the American people in his 2021 letter, adding that many presidents had simply governed as Democrats or Republicans without changing history, but the president told Biden, quote, This will not happen to you. Former President Biden describes the letter as if there were two Donald Trumps, a contrast to Trump's public attacks, he says. ”
Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America" is slated for a November 17th release.

RUSSELL WILSON WAS NEARLY THE CLEVELAND #BROWNS FRANCHISE QUARTERBACK…

Russell Wilson would have become the face of the Cleveland Browns, while Josh Allen could have spent his entire career with the Seattle Seahawks.

Instead, Cleveland went with Mayfield, eventually traded him, and later made the blockbuster move to acquire Deshaun Watson.

Seattle eventually traded Wilson to Denver in 2022.

text:
On Saturday night, 28 November 1992, around 21:50, APLA terrorists (the armed wing of the PAC) carried out a deliberate military-style attack on a year-end Christmas dinner of the King William’s Town Wine Circle at the King William’s Town Golf Club.

About 55–60 diners, ordinary people, including older couples, local residents, and the local National Party MP Ray Radue and his wife were seated in the dining hall enjoying their meal. Others were in the adjoining bar. This was not a political rally or security force gathering. It was a wine-tasting club’s festive dinner.

The attackers (led by Tembelani Xundu and including Sichumiso Nonxuba and others) entered the building. They rolled hand grenades into the dining hall and bar, then opened fire with R4 and R5 assault rifles. More fire and petrol bombs came from outside. The attack lasted only moments but turned the clubhouse into a slaughterhouse. Blood covered the floor and tables. A grenade blew a hole in the floor. Shrapnel and flying glass tore through people. Witnesses described absolute carnage.

Ian MacDonald (62) and his wife Rhoda MacDonald had moved to South Africa from Zimbabwe after independence. Ian worked for the Ciskei small-business development corporation; Rhoda was a nurse.

David Davis and his wife Gillian Davis were among the slaughtered.

Two couples wiped out while sitting at dinner.

Seventeen others were wounded. Injuries came from gunfire, grenade shrapnel, and flying glass. Some were serious. Among the survivors who later gave statements were Beth Savage who was seriously injured and left with lasting psychological trauma. She later said she wanted to meet the man who threw the grenade in a spirit of forgiveness.
Robert “Bob” Stanford was so badly wounded he required eight operations, was admitted to a mental institution, and was later barred from practicing as a lawyer.

The attackers escaped in a stolen white Volkswagen Jetta. APLA claimed responsibility by phone to police. A large reward was offered. The PAC later treated it as a political act targeting “White” civilians to force political change. The TRC Amnesty Committee granted amnesty in 2001 to Xundu, Malusi Morrison, Thobela Mlambisa, and Lungisa Ntintili after they claimed they acted under orders from Letlapa Mphahlele (APLA Director of Operations). The weapons came from the APLA regional commander in Umtata.

 The killers walked free under the TRC while the victims and their families were left with the graves and the lifelong damage.

This was not “resistance.” It was a calculated attack on White civilians at a social dinner in a public place, one of the early examples of the pattern of targeting soft White civilian gatherings that continued for years. The same ideology that said all Whites were legitimate targets did not end in 1994.

text:
Ilhan Omar Smiles Through Federal Probe, Tells Fox News "Have a Good Day" After Dodging Key Questions

Rep. Ilhan Omar brushed off reporters in a Capitol hallway this week as she faces an escalating federal investigation into possible immigration fraud involving her citizenship and family records. The Minnesota Democrat answered just one question before shutting down the exchange and walking away.

A Fox News reporter asked whether she had spoken with Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries about the probe at all. She offered no response. When pressed on whether the investigation was distracting her from representing her constituents, Omar replied, "I am not. Thank you."

The reporter followed up: "Any chance you'll step down as it plays out?" Omar smiled, said "Have a good day," and ended the conversation.

Federal agents searched Omar's Washington, D.C. home last month, seized her phone, and issued subpoenas to family members as part of a Justice Department inquiry examining whether false statements were made on immigration paperwork related to her age and naturalization from Somalia. She has denied wrongdoing and called the probe political intimidation. The clip shows her remaining unconcerned and unwilling to address leadership talks or resignation while the case continues.
